atlas-vn.0056: Techcombank’s Future Gen runs 24 months with rotations through business blocks and mentoring by senior leaders; Vietcombank asks for graduates of full-time or affiliated programmes only and treats a master’s as a priority criterion; BIDV recruits customer-relationship managers for foreign-invested clients in Korean and Chinese.
atlas-vn.0057: KPMG took 215 graduates from more than 4,000 applications in one October (2014) across Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Phnom Penh, with a 4-week induction and professional qualifications (ACCA, CPA Australia, VACPA) offered after 12 months. We could not open a 2026 graduate page for the Big Four.
atlas-vn.0058: Grant Thornton Hanoi wants fluent English, computer literacy and a 3-month internship, and applications go by email with a recent photo and transcript attached.
atlas-vn.0059: FPT Software hires final-year students and recent IT graduates as freshers through a paid training programme of 3 to 6 months, asking for English equivalent to TOEIC 700+; Viettel Digital Talent trains technology interns and some become employees while still studying.
atlas-vn.0060: The British Council survey found unmet demand for graduates with advanced IT, coding, digital-marketing and English skills, and VnEconomy (August 2026) reports annual IT shortages of 150,000 to 200,000 workers.
atlas-vn.0061: Programmes recruit from February to June (Viettel, FPT, Vietcombank, BIDV), accounting internships can close the September before, and experienced hiring peaks after Tet; there is no single national season.
atlas-vn.0062: Vietcombank treats a master’s or higher as a priority criterion. Against that, a practitioner quoted in the British Council report warns that a master’s straight after a bachelor’s, with no work experience and higher salary expectations, can count against you.
atlas-vn.0063: Foreign degrees are recognised by the Quality Management Department of the Ministry of Education and Training (Circular 13/2021, amended by Circular 07/2024) at the request of the holder or an employer; it takes up to 20 working days, or 45 if the foreign institution must verify. The page does not say how often employers ask for it.
atlas-vn.0064: Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track is open only to graduates of six named universities, and 88% of the 150 employers surveyed in 2018 agreed that studying overseas adds value; Viettel and FPT name no school.
atlas-vn.0065: We found no apprenticeship or dual-study route into graduate jobs; the structured routes are trainee programmes and internships. This is our reading.
atlas-vn.0066: Vietcombank and BIDV recruit graduates in national waves. The British Council report, citing a 2015 World Bank paper, puts state salaries at about 30% of the median wage and says this may deter overseas graduates from public-sector work; we found no figure for the public sector’s share of graduate hires, so the weight is our reading.
atlas-vn.0067: A fresh graduate does not meet the foreign-expert test (a degree plus 2 years of relevant experience, 1 year in technology, digital transformation and finance), and the graduate programmes read do not mention visas. See Visas for the rules. This is our reading.
atlas-vn.0068: Grant Thornton Hanoi asks for a recent photo attached to the application; the VietnamWorks pages read do not mention photos. This is our reading.
atlas-vn.0069: VietnamWorks’s CV guide ties a second page to substantial experience and suggests trimming to one page when it cannot be filled; Grant Thornton asks for the application and CV in English, under 2MB in total.
atlas-vn.0070: VietnamWorks lets each employer mark the cover letter Required, Optional or Not Required; the programme pages read (Viettel, FPT, Grant Thornton, Vietcombank) do not mention one.
atlas-vn.0071: Grant Thornton asks for the transcript attached to the application, and Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track asks for language and IT certificates. The pages read do not ask for certified or translated copies at application. This is our reading.
atlas-vn.0072: None of the programme pages read states a salary or asks for an expectation; FPT’s fresher post lists the training salary as “being updated”. This is our reading.
atlas-vn.0073: We found nothing on routine reference checks. A foreign hire needs a criminal-record certificate valid under 6 months, a legalised degree and a medical check for the work permit. See Visas.
atlas-vn.0074: Programmes take open online applications in large numbers, yet returning graduates reported having no contacts to lean on, so both apply. This is our reading of the sources.
atlas-vn.0075: Viettel’s 2026 intake took applications from 13 countries, but the foreign-worker route needs 2 years of experience and takes 8 to 12 weeks, and the visa-free stay does not allow work. See Visas.
atlas-vn.0076: Vietnamese for local firms and the programme pages read; English is asked for in the better graduate roles (FPT TOEIC 700+, Vietcombank IELTS 7.0 on one track) and 77% of foreign companies called it particularly important.
atlas-vn.0077: Vietcombank’s regular route in 2026 was two rounds, a professional-knowledge exam then an interview; outstanding graduates skip the exam. Grant Thornton Hanoi uses a technical test, or an IQ test and an English test for those exempt from it, then an interview.
atlas-vn.0078: FPT Software contacts only the selected candidates by email after an online application, and trains them for 3 to 6 months; Techcombank says it looks for Ability, Aspiration and Commitment but does not describe its stages. The Viettel pages read do not describe theirs either.
atlas-vn.0079: We did not establish the typical time from application to offer, interview dress and punctuality norms, how common video interviews are, or whether the Vietnamese programmes use assessment centres.
atlas-vn.0080: A written contract is required except for jobs under one month; it is indefinite-term or fixed-term up to 36 months (renewable once). Probation is up to 60 days for jobs needing a college degree or higher, pay during it must be at least 85% of the normal salary, and no notice is needed to end it.
atlas-vn.0081: Notice is 45 days on an indefinite contract, 30 days on a fixed term of 1 to 3 years and 3 working days for seasonal work. After 12 months, severance is generally half a month’s salary per year of service, with final payments within 14 working days.
atlas-vn.0082: A thirteenth-month salary is customary but not required by law; the regional minimum wage is VND 3,700,000 to 5,310,000 a month in 2026, the standard week is 48 hours and paid leave is 12 days after 12 months. Average monthly income of employees was VND 9 million in the first half of 2026.
atlas-vn.0083: In the 2018 survey, 33% of employers had failed to fill positions because the pay they offered missed candidates’ expectations, and 56% said local graduates ask for less; this points to salary being discussed. We did not establish whether graduates negotiate or how long employers give to decide.
atlas-vn.0084: A foreign expert needs a university degree plus 2 years of relevant experience (1 year in science and technology, digital transformation, semiconductors, AI or strategic finance), so a fresh graduate generally does not qualify. The employer must advertise the post for 5 working days and file with DOLISA; the statutory time is about 35 working days, in practice 8 to 12 weeks.
atlas-vn.0085: Foreign students currently enrolled with an internship agreement or a job offer from a Vietnamese entity are exempt from the work permit once DOLISA certifies it, at no state fee. The employer must apply for the certificate, so ask early.
atlas-vn.0086: Entering visa-free (45 days for citizens of 18 EU countries and the UK) allows visits and interviews but not work; working without the permit risks expulsion and a fine of VND 15 to 25 million. Legalised degrees and a criminal-record certificate under 6 months old are needed. Whether employers will do all this for a new graduate is our reading: the sources do not say.
atlas-vn.0087: Portals: VietnamWorks (run by Navigos Group), ITviec for IT jobs (English and Vietnamese) and CareerViet; BIDV applies through its recruitment portal (tuyendung.bidv.com.vn).
atlas-vn.0088: Employer programmes: Viettel Talent (Viettel Digital Talent and Viettel Future Changemakers), Techcombank Future Gen, FPT Software’s fresher programme, Vietcombank’s branch waves and Grant Thornton’s internships.
atlas-vn.0089: University fairs and services: HUTECH’s technology and recruitment day (7 May 2026) in Ho Chi Minh City; for others, follow your university’s career or student office, since fairs are announced a few weeks ahead.
atlas-vn.0090: Recruitment firms such as Adecco Vietnam work with clients that value overseas-educated graduates.
atlas-vn.0091: Applying too late: Grant Thornton Hanoi’s January internship closed on 17 September, Viettel opened registration on 12 February and Vietcombank and BIDV closed in mid-June 2026.
atlas-vn.0092: Treating English as a formality: FPT asks for TOEIC 700+ equivalent, Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track for IELTS 7.0 or equivalent, and Grant Thornton adds an English test.
atlas-vn.0093: Starting work on a visa-free stay: it does not allow work, and working without the permit risks expulsion and a fine of VND 15 to 25 million.
atlas-vn.0094: Overpricing yourself after a degree abroad: 33% of the 150 employers surveyed in 2018 had failed to fill a post over salary expectations.
atlas-vn.0095: Re-applying or sending a second CV on VietnamWorks: it takes one CV per application and does not let you change it or re-apply to the same job.
atlas-vn.0096: Counting on a thirteenth-month salary or Tet bonus: neither is required by law, so look for it in the contract.
